coder_notes: Season 22 is about one perpetrator, a young Indiana woman whose scams, impersonations and false accusations affected many people (her name is withheld throughout and replaced by [perpetrator] in quotes). Most of the season is told by community members (a Facebook 'scam awareness' group) and the host rather than by those harmed; many victims never spoke. Community members' work was mostly in finding her after she skipped bond: (1) an Aug 12, 2023 sting where police released her because the only warrant then was a non-extraditable bench warrant from the OWI case ('they basically just let her go', s22-e7 @ 31:42) - this concerned her OWI, not any harmed person's case, so it is not coded as a contact; (2) the Sept 2023 arrest after a fake practitioner account located her, coded under the rental-scam victims. Not coded as persons: Chloe, Justin, Alex Brewster, Lainey, Amanda, Hannah, Mike Neal (participants whose 'harm' was deceit, faked campaign data, co-opted stories or wasted effort; none describe institutional contact on their own harm), the Todd Young/Curtis Hill campaigns and the Madison County GOP (organizations), iTown children's gift drive (the church bought the gifts; no child harmed). The falsely accused Speaker and others are listed in others_mentioned without names because of the accused-person rule. Group records were used for the three charged rental victims and the pastor couple because the season tells each group's story together. E13 (Celisia Stanton, a different perpetrator) and a WCN/What Came Next crossover about Madison McGhee's father (found inside s22_07/s22_08) are coded as separate stories. The perpetrator's own statements (e.g., repaying victims, the aunt dropping her suit) are flagged as such. Reading was interrupted by usage limits several times; I resumed at the next unread line each time, and all eight files were read to their last line.
